name: Maine Tool Library
whatItIs: A lending library for tools instead of books — gardening, landscaping, home-improvement, and kitchen tools you can check out for a week.
whoItsFor: DIY-ers, gardeners, and renters doing a one-off home project without buying tools.
howToAccess: Visit during open hours (Tue / Thu / Sat) at 224 Anderson St, or sign up online to become a member, then borrow tools on a weekly loan.

name: Library Museum & Park Passes
whatItIs: Free passes the Portland Public Library lends out to museums, state parks, and cultural sites — the Portland Museum of Art, Coastal Maine Botanical Gardens, Maine State Parks, and more.
whoItsFor: Families, students, and anyone wanting a free museum or park day.
howToAccess: Reserve a pass in the library catalog or call (207) 871-1700 x730, then pick it up at your branch.

name: Library of Things
whatItIs: Beyond books, the Portland Public Library lends everyday gear — mobile Wi-Fi hotspots, microscopes, and telescope / night-sky kits — with your library card.
whoItsFor: Students, hobbyists, and travelers who need a gadget for a short time.
howToAccess: Browse the catalog, place a hold on the item, and pick it up at your branch with your library card.

name: Public EV Charging Stations
whatItIs: City-owned electric-vehicle chargers at downtown garages and lots — free to use while you're parked.
cost: Free to charge; garage parking fees apply ($3–$5/hr)
howToAccess: Drive up to a city charger (Elm, Spring, or Temple St garage, Payson Park, or City Hall) and plug in while parked.

name: Community Gardens
whatItIs: Ten neighborhood garden sites the city runs with Cultivating Community, where residents can rent a plot to grow their own food.
whoItsFor: Residents who want space to grow vegetables and flowers.
howToAccess: Apply for a plot through the city / Cultivating Community, and join the waitlist if your neighborhood garden is full.

name: Public Boat Launch
whatItIs: A public, all-tides boat ramp at East End Beach on the Eastern Promenade, for launching recreational boats and kayaks on Casco Bay.
cost: $5 day-use fee for trailered boats; free to hand-carry a kayak in
howToAccess: Launch at East End Beach off the Eastern Promenade and pay the $5 day-use fee at the self-pay station if a ranger isn't present.

name: Bulky-Item Pickup
whatItIs: Public Works curbside collection for large items that won't fit in a trash bag — furniture, appliances, mattresses, and most electronics.
whoItsFor: Residents clearing out furniture, appliances, or electronics.
cost: Free for items ≤30 lbs (limit 10/year); $40 per heavier item
howToAccess: Apply for a Bulky Waste Permit online first, then set the items curbside on your scheduled collection day.

name: Composting & Recycling
whatItIs: The city's curbside recycling program plus guidance on what's accepted and how to keep food scraps and yard waste out of the trash.
cost: Free curbside recycling; Pay-As-You-Throw bags for trash
howToAccess: Set recycling curbside on your collection day, and check the guide for accepted materials and composting options.

name: Board & Commission Seats
whatItIs: Open volunteer seats on the city's boards and commissions — from historic preservation to the police review board — listed and applied for through OnBoardGOV.
whoItsFor: Residents who want a real say in city decisions.
howToAccess: Browse open seats on OnBoardGOV and apply online; contact the City Clerk with questions.

name: Public Meeting Rooms
whatItIs: Bookable rooms and study pods at the Portland Public Library that community groups and small teams can use.
whoItsFor: Community groups, nonprofits, and study groups.
howToAccess: Check room availability and rates on the library's Room Rentals page, or call the Reference Desk at (207) 871-1700 x725 about study pods.
